rationale: The expectation the lane's fixture source was written against, authored from the CONTRACT the source's own doc comments state (five construction surfaces for `instantiates`, the read/callee/write/attribute-argument exclusions for `uses`) and from the naming conventions the four sibling fixtures already pinned: a member read is `uses` on the MEMBER name, a bare receiver names nothing, a dotted path is one edge per segment the file reads, and an attribute argument names a symbol for the compiler rather than reading it. The source predates this file and its comments are the specification; nothing here was copied from analyzer output, and the run after authoring is the test of the analyzer against that specification. `meta.constructsArray` is pinned exactly where the source demands the distinction (`New Gauge()` is an object_creation, `New Gauge(1)` and `New Integer(10)` arrive through the array-shaped node the grammar gives every construction with arguments, and the source says the edge must record which node produced it rather than pretend the two are one thing).

expectSymbols.name: operator
expectSymbols.comment: the contract literal, as in declaration-shapes: `Operator =` has no name field, so the name is `operator`

expectRelationships.comment: SURFACE 1: `New Gauge()` is an `object_creation_expression` with the name in a `type` field and no `function` field, so the callee must be read the way a construction is read, not the way an invocation is read.

SURFACE 2: `New Gauge(1)` is an ARRAY CREATION in this grammar -- the same node type a real array construction produces -- so a visitor keyed on `object_creation_expression` alone misses it. `constructsArray` records which node produced the edge instead of pretending the two are one thing.

SURFACE 3: `As New T` is a construction with NO EXPRESSION around it -- it hangs off the declaration's own `as_clause`, so it is reachable only from the declaration visitor and from nowhere an expression walk looks. The source attribution for a field initializer is the containing TYPE, the same attribution the ontology fixture pins for `Builds -> Timer`.

SURFACE 4: an ARRAY construction over a PREDEFINED type. `Integer` is never a project symbol, so this edge is the heuristic-confidence one -- the two facts are different: 'this file constructs a type it declares' and 'this file allocates an array of a type it does not'.

SURFACE 5: a construction inside an OPERATOR. The operator's own symbol is the contract literal `operator`, so the edge is sourced at a name a consumer can navigate to -- a source that is a keyword would not be.
USES 1, the shape that IS a use: `Me.Reading` is a value read that is neither a call nor a write. `Reading` is declared in this file, so the edge carries the resolved confidence.

USES 4, the chained call: `a.Inner().Reading` puts the leading segment under a node the climb has to pass THROUGH, or `Inner` is published as a read of a member that is being CALLED. `Reading` at the end of the chain is the real use.

USES 5a: the middle segment of `Metrics.Counter.Total`. The receiver `Metrics` is a bare identifier and names nothing; `Counter` is a segment the file reads, published at the heuristic confidence because a bare member name is project-ambiguous and only this file could have resolved it.
USES 5b: the read of the LAST segment on a receiver this file does NOT declare. The edge is still published, because the read is real, at the heuristic confidence.

forbidRelationships.comment: USES 2, the shape that is NOT a use: `obj.Method()` is a CALL, and publishing the receiver's member as a read too would put one line under two types -- which is how a `calls` count and a `uses` count drift apart.

USES 3, the shape that is NOT a use: `obj.Member = x` is a WRITE. The definition is a read that is neither a call nor a write; an assignment's left side is the other side of that sentence. Scoped to WriteOnce so the legitimate ReadOnce read of the same member is untouched.
the callee half of USES 4: `Inner` is being CALLED, so it belongs to `calls` and not to `uses` -- the same exclusion CalleeIsNotARead and Invoked pin in the ontology fixture.

AN ATTRIBUTE ARGUMENT IS NOT A MEMBER READ. `<Obsolete(Marker)>` names a symbol FOR THE COMPILER; publishing `uses -> Marker` off the declaration it is written on would claim the declaration reads itself.
control: the receiver of the dotted read is a bare identifier and names nothing -- the same rule that keeps `System` out of the Utf8 chain in the ontology fixture.

knownResidual: `uses` targets are the NAME the file reads and not a resolved symbol, so `Counter` and `Total` resolve at the heuristic confidence a cross-file name always carries; that is the honest number for this shape, not a defect (the lane's ontology fixture records the same residual). The `instantiates` rows here pin the contract for five surfaces; whether the analyzer satisfies them is what the run after authoring decides, and a failing row is a defect finding to be probed and fixed, never a row to be edited to match output.
